title: A Extraction for the Drop
premise: Kestrel Nakamura, a financial whistle-blower living under four identities, discovers her safe house listed online with interior photos — proof someone knows exactly who and where she is. The listing is bait set by a fixer working for the hedge fund she exposed, timed to an 'accident' scheduled to erase her testimony before Frankfurt markets open. Forced out of hiding, Kestrel must ally with the last person she trusts — the investigator hired to find her — to expose the plot in real time. In the end, she chooses truth over survival, testifying live as the attack unfolds, surviving by making herself too public to kill.
about_author: Juniper Eastwick is a former compliance analyst who spent a decade inside the quiet machinery of global finance before trading it for fiction. She writes paranoid, propulsive thrillers about people whose names no longer belong to them.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Bag
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A routine morning ritual: rotating identities, checking exits, rehearsing her cover story aloud. She notices a realtor's flyer wedged in the door of her safe house — open house Saturday. The emotional beat is the first crack of dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Kestrel finds the property online: photos of her kitchen, her go-bag half-visible under the bed, her burner phone on the counter. Someone photographed the inside. POV shifts briefly to the anonymous buyer's agent watching the page views climb. Beat: violation and vertigo.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: Kestrel executes her escape plan but hesitates over one item: evidence against Meridian Capital she never finished distributing. Flashbacks establish the whistle-blowing that put four names between her and her old life. Beat: grief for the self she erased.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers the Door
chapters.summary: Investigator Elias Voss arrives at the empty safe house following a missing-persons contract — and finds Kestrel waiting in his rental car. Their charged negotiation reveals he was hired not to find her but to confirm her location for someone else. Beat: uneasy alliance born of mutual leverage.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. They return to the safe house during the open house to trace who booked it. A fake couple tours the rooms with measuring eyes; Kestrel recognizes professional surveillance tradecraft. They barely slip away. Beat: hunted, together, for the first time.

chapters.title: Meridian's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel decodes the encrypted files she's carried for two years: evidence that Meridian plans to trigger a catastrophic 'accident' at a Frankfurt data center before markets open Monday, erasing audit trails and her testimony alike. Beat: the personal threat becomes a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Contact Ghost
chapters.summary: Kestrel reaches her old handler through a dead-drop protocol, only to learn he vanished three weeks ago. His last message: 'They bought the building.' POV alternates with the fixer, Anselm Roth, reporting progress to Meridian. Beat: isolation deepens; the enemy gains a face.

chapters.title: Train to Basel
chapters.summary: A tense rail journey to meet a journalist who once sat on Kestrel's story. Voss covers her trail while wrestling with his own contract — deliver her, or protect her? Onboard, Kestrel spots a tail. Beat: trust tested at speed; loyalty vs. truth crystallizes between them.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Waited
chapters.summary: In Basel, journalist Mara Osei reveals she never published because Meridian buried the story with legal warfare — and because Kestrel disappeared mid-verification. Mara agrees to run it if Kestrel goes on record, live, from Frankfurt. Beat: the cost of invisibility made explicit.

chapters.title: Roth Closes In
chapters.summary: Anselm Roth's POV. He identifies the Basel contact and sets a trap disguised as a safe-house offer. Kestrel, sensing the too-clean logistics, refuses at the last moment — but Mara is taken instead. Beat: guilt; the hunt turns predatory.

chapters.title: What Voss Knows
chapters.summary: Voss confesses: his client dossier included Kestrel's real name from day one, and he took the job to get close to Meridian, who destroyed his brother's pension fund. Two liars, one target. Beat: raw honesty as the alliance becomes something like loyalty.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, Friday Night
chapters.summary: The pair infiltrate Meridian's Frankfurt office using credentials Voss still holds. They find the accident's blueprint: a gas-line 'failure' timed for 8:45 a.m., wiping the archive floor where Kestrel's original documents are stored. Beat: cold clarity — the attack is also an erasure of evidence.

chapters.title: Mara's Voice
chapters.summary: A proof-of-life call: Roth offers a trade — Kestrel for Mara, midnight, a freight yard. Kestrel insists on going despite Voss's objection. Flashback to her father teaching her that running is a skill, not a life. Beat: belonging asserted; she refuses to spend people to save herself.

chapters.title: Freight Yard Midnight
chapters.summary: The exchange sours into ambush. Kestrel springs a counter-trap using the yard's own cameras, freeing Mara but exposing her face to Roth's lens. Voss takes a bullet grazing his side covering their exit. Beat: victory priced in exposure and blood.

chapters.title: Four Names, Zero Left
chapters.summary: Roth floods every channel with Kestrel's photograph and true identity. Her four lives collapse within hours — bank cards dead, contacts burning, safe houses compromised. Hiding in a laundromat basement, she realizes invisibility was always Meridian's gift, now revoked. Beat: identity stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: The Only Weapon Left
chapters.summary: Kestrel reframes the game: if she can't hide, she'll be unmissable. Plan formed — go live on Mara's stream at 8:30 a.m., outside the data center, telling everything before the 'accident' can look accidental. Voss volunteers as her shield. Beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Sunday Vigil
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter. The trio prepares: statements memorized, contingencies drawn, Mara's uplink tested. Kestrel writes letters to the people from her discarded lives, then burns them. Voss and Kestrel share an unspoken almost-promise. Beat: stillness before the storm; belonging found in two allies.

chapters.title: 8:29 A.M.
chapters.summary: Monday. Kestrel steps before the cameras outside the data center and begins speaking as Roth's crew moves into position inside. Markets tremble; Meridian's lawyers scramble; viewership climbs past the point where an 'accident' becomes implausible. Beat: exposure as armor.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Roth triggers the sabotage early rather than abort. Kestrel narrates live as alarms erupt behind her; emergency crews arrive to a building already famous. Voss physically blocks Roth's extraction team until police swarm. Beat: climax — truth outrunning the match.

chapters.title: Roth's Last Client
chapters.summary: Captured, Roth reveals Meridian's chairman ordered the hit personally — and that Kestrel's handler is alive, held as leverage against exactly this scenario. A raid frees him. Beat: catharsis with a hook; the conspiracy has a head left to cut.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Kestrel testifies under her real name — spoken aloud for the first time in years — as regulators freeze Meridian and markets digest the fallout. Voss waits outside, no longer under contract. Beat: identity reclaimed; loyalty rewarded without erasing its costs.

chapters.title: One Name, No Bag
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Kestrel's POV. She unpacks the go-bag at last in a small apartment with her name on the lease. A new listing alert pings — a house for sale, ordinary, hers to choose. She smiles, closes the laptop, and stays. Beat: resolution — belonging chosen, not hidden into.
